title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Sofia Chen
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for core cross-functional processes: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and reusable internal templates. It is intended for managers, approvers, and process owners across engineering, product, finance, security, and people-ops.

Owners and scope

- Primary owner: people-ops (policy oversight, updates, annual reviews)
- Co-owners: finance-legal (procurement & vendor contracts), security (access/RBAC and data controls), eng-sre (change management and eng runbooks)
- Applies to: all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors with access to Redwood systems or company funds.

1) Access and permissions

Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, consistent onboarding/offboarding, and documented ownership for all access grants.

Key controls and standards:

- Identity provider: Redwood uses Okta for SSO and SCIM provisioning. All user accounts must be created via Okta.
- Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Standard roles are defined in the RBAC catalog (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth). Teams must map service-specific roles to catalog roles during onboarding.
- Privileged access: Administrative roles (cloud admin, database admin, PKI/KMS admin) require manager + security approval and a completed Justification Form. Access must be approved via the Access Request workflow in Jira (project: INFRA-ACCESS).
- Temporary access: Temporary elevated access is granted for a maximum of 7 days. Requests must state the business reason, duration, and approval chain. Audit log entries are required for all temporary grants.
- Onboarding checklist (people-ops + team manager):
  1. Create Okta account and assign baseline groups (employee/contractor).
  2. Provision required platform roles using SCIM mappings.
  3. Enroll in MFA (we require hardware tokens for privileged roles).
  4. Complete security training and sign acceptable-use policy.
  5. Confirm mailbox and expense access (Finance).
- Offboarding steps (to be initiated on termination notice):
  1. Revoke Okta access (immediately for terminated-for-cause).
  2. Deprovision cloud console roles (AWS/GCP/Azure) via cloud-accounts-and-networking runbook.
  3. Rotate any shared keys or credentials the person had access to.
  4. Archive relevant artifacts to a designated location.
- Access review cadence: Quarterly team-level reviews required. Team leads must publish a signed review record to /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging.

2) Change management

Purpose: Maintain safe, auditable rollouts for infra, runtime, and customer-impacting changes.

Scope: Configuration changes (networking, VPCs, IAM policies), runtime changes (serving runtime kernel updates, model version promotion), production database schema migrations, and console/API breaking changes.

Process highlights:

- Change types and approval thresholds:
  - Standard change (low-risk routine): documented in a ticket, peer-reviewed, deployable via CI. No CAB required.
  - Major change (config/infra/runtime with customer impact): requires test plan, rollback plan, and CAB approval (Change Advisory Board: eng-platform, eng-sre, security, product).
  - Emergency change: follow the oncall-and-incident-response emergency change runbook; retrospective required within 3 business days.
- Required artifacts for major changes:
  - PRD or design doc link, impact analysis, test/benchmark results, SLO impact estimate, rollback steps, and nominated owner.
- Deployment windows and blackout periods:
  - Regular deployments allowed during business hours 02:00-10:00 UTC unless otherwise justified.
  - Blackout: end-of-quarter and customer release blackout 48 hours before major customer-facing launch.
- Rollout patterns recommended:
  - Canary -> Gradual traffic ramp -> A/B rollback window (48 hours) -> Full promotion.
  - Automatic rollback threshold: error rate > 2x baseline or p95 latency > 2x SLO for 15 minutes.
- Post-deployment verification: health-check pass, smoke-test assertions, and a post-deploy checklist filed in the deploy ticket.

3) Data management

Purpose: Protect customer data, comply with retention policies, and ensure reproducible datasets for evals and audits.

Policies and procedures:

- Data classification: All data must be labeled at creation as Public, Internal, or Restricted. Restricted data includes PII, customer-provided data under NDA, and export-controlled materials.
- Data access rules:
  - Restricted data requires explicit data owner approval and justification. Access is limited via IAM roles and data access request tickets.
  - Storage services: primary data lakes are hosted in AWS S3 with encryption at rest (AES-256) and in transit via TLS 1.2+.
- Retention and deletion:
  - Default retention for logs: 90 days (hot), 2 years (cold).
  - Customer data retention follows contract terms; minimum retention is 30 days unless longer required.
  - Secure deletion: when retention expires or contract ends, run the purge job documented in /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention.
- Data lifecycle for evaluations and model onboarding:
  - Use dedicated sandbox buckets and ephemeral compute for evals. No production customer data in eval sandboxes.
  - All archived eval datasets must include provenance metadata (source, owner, hash) and a review entry from applied-ml-and-evals.
- Incident handling (data exposure): follow incident-response-security procedures and notify legal/people-ops within 24 hours of discovery.

4) Procurement and expenses

Purpose: Provide clear thresholds and procedures that balance speed of purchase with appropriate financial controls.

Procurement thresholds and routing:

- Low-value purchases (<= $2,000): team lead approval, purchase via company credit card or expense report.
- Mid-value purchases ($2,001- $50,000): require finance-legal approval and a purchase requisition in Coupa (or authorized procurement system).
- High-value purchases (> $50,000): require director-level approval, finance-legal review, and, for multi-year commitments, legal contracting.
- Cloud spend commitments and Dedicated capacity reservations: procurement must be coordinated with eng-sre and product-finance to estimate utilization and commit tiers.

Expense policy highlights:

- Reimbursement timeline: submit receipts within 30 days; finance processes reimbursements on a biweekly payroll cycle.
- Personal charges: personal items on a company card must be repaid within 7 days.
- Corporate card usage: program cards are assigned to managers; unusual card usage triggers an audit and manager notification.

Template checklist for procurements:

1. Business justification (1-2 paragraphs)
2. Budget code and owner
3. Vendor contact and W-9 / tax documentation
4. Estimated total cost and recurring vs one-time breakdown
5. Risk analysis (data access, vendor continuity, security posture)
6. Required approvals (list names and titles)

5) Vendor management

Purpose: Ensure vendors meet security, financial, and operational standards before onboarding and during the contract lifecycle.

Vendor onboarding steps:

1. Initial vendor questionnaire (security and compliance basics) completed by vendor and reviewed by security.
2. Legal reviews standard contract terms; exceptions require director-level signoff.
3. Finance completes credit / payment terms review and assigns vendor code.
4. Security performs a risk assessment for vendors with access to Restricted data or systems.
5. Contract is stored in the Contracts repository with an assigned contract owner and renewal reminder (45 days before expiry).

Vendor monitoring and offboarding:

- Quarterly vendor reviews for critical vendors (hosting, infra, and data processors).
- SLA monitoring: vendors must provide at least 99.9% uptime for critical infra services unless otherwise contracted. Escalation path must be documented in vendor-specific runbooks.
- Offboarding checklist: revoke access, collect assets, verify data deletion or return, and close the contract in the system.

6) Travel policy

Principles: Safety, cost-effectiveness, and fairness. Business travel should be pre-approved and aligned with budgets.

Booking and approvals:

- All travel requires a travel request with manager approval submitted at least 7 business days before travel. Exceptions possible for emergencies.
- Preferred booking channels: company travel portal (Concur) or approved travel agency.
- Class of travel: domestic flights: economy; international flights > 6 hours: premium economy or coach plus; executive exceptions require VP approval.
- Lodging: mid-range hotels (4-star or equivalent). Use negotiated corporate rates where available.

Per diems and reimbursable items:

- Daily per diem: $75 domestic, $125 international (covers meals & incidentals).
- Reimbursable: airfare, ground transport to/from airports, lodging, registration fees for conferences, visa fees. Receipts required for all reimbursements except per-diem.
- Non-reimbursable: personal leisure charges, alcohol above local per-diem unless client entertainment pre-approved.

Safety and incident reporting:

- In case of emergency while traveling, contact people-ops and the local emergency contact in the travel portal.
- Travel insurance: Redwood provides travel insurance for all approved international trips.

7) Internal templates and forms

This section centralizes commonly used templates and where to find them. Use these templates for consistency and auditability.

Key templates (all available in the Templates directory):

- Access Justification Form (templates/access-justification.md)
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (templates/vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx)
- Purchase Requisition Template (templates/purchase-requisition.xlsx)
- Travel Request Form (templates/travel-request-form.pdf)
- Change Request Checklist (templates/change-request-checklist.md)
- Offboarding checklist (templates/offboarding-checklist.md)

Template governance:

- Templates are owned by people-ops or the functional owner (security, finance); changes require reviewer approval from the owning team.
- Versioning: all templates must include a version footer (e.g., v2026-10-01) and a changelog entry in the template header.

Governance, exceptions, and review cadence

- Exception process: Any request to deviate from these policies must be documented in an Exception Request ticket, include business rationale, mitigation plan, and be approved by the policy owner and an executive (director or above).
- Review cadence: People-ops will run an annual policy review in Q4. Security and finance will run targeted reviews quarterly for their domains.
